subject: Re: Acme - Long-context evals & model fit follow-up

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme - Long-context evals & next steps

Hi Samir / Lily,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Primary goal: robust, faithful summarization of long technical documents (meeting minutes, RFCs, and client reports) without losing critical action items.
- Target context: many docs are ~30-60k tokens; some aggregated threads can hit ~100k tokens.
- Success metrics you called out: summarization fidelity (ROUGE/QA pass rate), truncation behavior (no dropped action items), and latency SLOs ~500-800ms per query at P95 for interactive workflows.
- Throughput: initial volume is small (pilot 10k queries/month) with spikes during quarter close.

Next steps we discussed:
1) You to share a representative sample (redacted) of ~20 docs.
2) We'll run a 3-model long-context evaluation (see proposed models below) against 3 prompt variants and the prompt set attached.
3) Deliverables: benchmarking report (truncation/rescue cases), prompt-set recommendations, and cost/latency estimates.

Preliminary ask from our side: can you confirm the dataset delivery by Friday (2026-08-06)? If that's tight, a subset of ~5-8 docs will work for an initial run.

Proposed models for the pilot (subject to resource constraints):
- redwood-long-70b-100k (native 100k context variant)
- redwood-13b-long (13B long-context optimized)
- redwood-7b-q4f32-long (quantized candidate for cost comparison)

I attached the prompt set we discussed (acme_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short evaluation plan. I'll follow up internally to get cost estimates and an eval window.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

On Wed, Aug 4, 2026 at 11:02 AM Samir Patel <samir@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa \u2014 this looks great. A few clarifying Qs before we hand over samples: 
> 
> 1) Which of the three models do you expect to be the best balance of fidelity vs cost for our use case? We care most about not dropping action items in summaries.
> 2) Do you have any benchmark docs that show truncation behavior (especially for documents >64k tokens)?
> 3) Can you give a rough cost estimate for a 1K-query pilot run?

Great questions. Short answers up front: the 70B long-context variant will likely give the best fidelity for edge cases (rare action items), the 13B-long is surprisingly strong for structured summaries and is a much lower cost baseline, and the 7B-q variant is for cost/latency trade-offs.

Details / links:
- Benchmarks: I attached a short benchmark PDF (acme_long_context_benchmarks.pdf) that demonstrates truncation/rescue behavior on synthetic documents up to 120k tokens. You can see the comparison of entity-loss metrics and QA pass rates across the three models.
- Truncation behavior: our runtime supports native >64k contexts in the redwood-long variants; when native context is not available we implement principled chunking + overlap and a KV-rescue heuristic to preserve action-item spans (results in the attached).
- Cost estimate (ballpark for 1K pilot queries with our batching defaults):
    \u2022 redwood-long-70b-100k: ~$6,000
    \u2022 redwood-13b-long: ~$1,200
    \u2022 redwood-7b-q4f32-long: ~$480
(We will provide precise estimates after seeing your actual average document length and required P95 latency.)

Quality regression note: for long-context workloads the main risks we monitor are (1) truncation-induced information loss, (2) prompt sensitivity across chunk boundaries, and (3) subtle hallucinations introduced by aggressive compression heuristics. Our eval will surface examples and recommend prompt/local post-processing to reduce these risks.

Deliverables: final report, per-prompt per-model metrics, and a \u201crescue examples\u201d appendix highlighting cases where action items were dropped or reformulated.

I've attached model profiles and the benchmark PDF. If this looks good I'll start the internal eval request and loop our infra folks for cost/slots. Would you like a 30-min sync next week to review results?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: acme_long_context_benchmarks.pdf, redwood_model_profiles.xlsx
